It’s more than I’d ever eat if someone were there with me. 

I always do it alone. I tell friends I’m too tired to meet for dinner, but really I don’t want anyone to see how I eat at night. I feel ashamed even thinking about it. 

Along with that, I’ve just felt… dulled out. I still teach, but I don’t get the same joy from my students’ progress or from playing for myself. On days when I don’t have many lessons, it’s hard to make myself practice or even leave the apartment, and I end up just waiting for the day to be over.

D023-D013_h024.question:
I guess this really started a few months after I got laid off. My days kind of blend together now. I’ll be fine for a while, then out of nowhere I get this urge to just…eat. It’s usually at night, when my wife has gone to bed. I’ll stand in the kitchen and go through whatever’s there—leftovers, bread, cereal, cookies—just one thing after another. I’m not even really hungry, but I keep going until my stomach actually hurts and I feel stuffed in a way that’s almost painful.

I don’t do it in front of my wife or kids. I wait until I’m alone because I feel ridiculous about how much I’m putting away. Sometimes I hide the wrappers so no one sees. Afterwards I feel heavy and kind of ashamed, like, “What’s wrong with me? Why can’t I just stop?”

Since losing my job I’ve been more down than usual—low energy, not much interest in anything, sleeping odd hours—but I’m not sure if that’s just stress. It comes and goes. The eating feels like the only thing that gives me a break from thinking about everything, at least in the moment.

D023-D013_h025.question:
I work nights at a data center, so my schedule’s pretty flipped. The eating stuff has been going on for… I’m not exactly sure, maybe a few months? It’s hard to track time on night shift.

On my breaks, especially on slower nights, I’ll go to the vending machines or grab takeout and just keep eating. It’s not like a normal meal; I’ll order way more than other guys I’m with and keep going even after I can feel my stomach stretching and kind of hurting. Sometimes I’m almost on autopilot, just shoving food in until I feel almost sick.

I usually do it when I’m alone—like I’ll wait until everyone’s back on the floor and then eat in the break room by myself, or in my car. I get really self-conscious about how much I’m putting away, so I’d rather nobody sees it.

Mood-wise, I’ve just been kind of low and drained. I’m not totally nonfunctional—I still go to work—but it feels like everything takes extra effort. Some nights the eating feels like the only thing I actually look forward to, and then afterward I end up feeling pretty lousy about myself.
